A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a large class of control systems, the null controllability properties are preserved under the perturbation of the control system by a dynamical one.
, under the irreducibility assumption, global null controllabilty holds for almost all paths.
, under the irreducibility assumption, the null controllability properties of the system are independent of the dynamics of the coefficients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global null controllabilty is not destroyed by the presence of positive Lyapounov exponent, as long as the system is irreducible.
the null controllability problem is robust with respect to the coefficients, provided the coefficients vary in a controlled manner.
, for linear control systems, the global null controllabilty is determined by the local null controllabililty and by the Lyapounv exponents of the associated uncontrolled system.
